entities.name: Qara Iskander
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Qara Iskander, whose name translates to 'Black Alexander,' led the Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep Turkomans) tribal confederation from 1420 until his death in 1436. Succeeding his formidable father Qara Yusuf, Iskander inherited a vast yet unstable domain stretching across parts of Anatolia, the Caucasus, and Persia. His reign is primarily defined by relentless, often desperate, military engagements against the resurgent Timurid Empire under Shah Rukh, a struggle that underscored the volatile geopolitical landscape of the early 15th-century Middle East and determined the fate of the Qara Qoyunlu as a dominant regional power.

Following his father's death in 1420, Iskander navigated a complex succession crisis, consolidating power against his brothers and other contenders. His early victories, particularly the fierce resistance against Shah Rukh's initial campaigns in Azerbaijan and Armenia, showcased his tactical acumen and personal courage, notably at the Battle of Alashkert in 1421. However, despite these localized successes, Iskander was consistently outmaneuvered by the superior resources and strategic depth of the Timurids. Shah Rukh launched three major campaigns into the Qara Qoyunlu territories (1420-21, 1427-29, 1434-36), each progressively weakening Iskander's authority and forcing him into retreat or submission, ultimately leading to the loss of key territories and the erosion of tribal loyalty.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Qara Iskander's 16-year reign marked a critical period of decline for the Qara Qoyunlu confederation, directly contributing to the eventual ascendancy of rival Turkoman powers and shaping the geopolitical landscape of 15th-century Persia and the Caucasus.
